question.problem:
Which of the following sets are orthogonal?

I. $U=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\}$

II. $V=\{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0 \\ -6\end{aligned}]\}$

III. $W=\{[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -10\end{aligned}]\}$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of the given sets as 
$\{{u}_{1},{u}_{2},{u}_{3}\},$ 
$\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\},$ and 
$\{{w}_{1},{w}_{2}\},$ respectively. 

The sets $U,V,$ and $W$ are orthogonal if the following conditions on each set hold:

- ${u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0,\,{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{3}=0,\,{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{3}=0.$

- ${v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2}=0,\,{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{3}=0,\,{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{3}=0.$

- ${w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2}=0.$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

- For the set $U,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=-1+0+1=0 & ✓ \\ {u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0+0+0=0 & ✓ \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0+0+0=0 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $U$ is orthogonal.

- For the set $V,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=12+0+1=13\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $V$ is not an orthogonal set.

- For the set $W,$ notice that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -10\end{aligned}]=-40+40=0 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $W$ is orthogonal.

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "$U$ and $W$ only".
